topic.label: Slavic Languages and Literatures
topic.desc: Slavic Languages and Literatures: Russian and other Slavic languages, their literatures, linguistics and cultural history.

concepts: Learning Russian pronunciation, Cyrillic script, case grammar and verbal aspect from beginning to advanced proficiency.
The structure and history of the Slavic languages: Proto-Slavic, Old Church Slavonic, phonology, morphology and dialects.
Russian literature from the medieval period through Pushkin, the nineteenth-century novel, Soviet literature and the present.
Polish, Czech, Ukrainian and South Slavic Literatures
Literatures and cultures of the West, East and South Slavic peoples beyond Russia.
Translating Slavic literary and non-literary texts into English and analyzing translation choices.
Intellectual, visual and political culture of Russia and Eastern Europe, including Orthodoxy, the avant-garde, Soviet film and post-Soviet media.
skills: Generates case-ending exercises for nouns and adjectives with answer keys checked against standard declension tables.
Explains perfective and imperfective choice in sentences and corrects learner errors, checked against grammar references.
Glosses a Russian text with stress marks, vocabulary and grammar notes for a proficiency level, checked for gloss accuracy.
Derives modern Slavic word forms from Proto-Slavic reconstructions through dated sound changes, checked against etymological dictionaries.
Parses Old Church Slavonic forms for morphology and translates them, checked against a reference grammar.
Compares phonology and morphology across Slavic languages and dialects, checked against cited descriptions.
Produces a close reading of a poem or passage with meter, imagery and context, checked against the original text.
Analyzes themes, narrative form and characters of a Russian novel, checked against cited criticism.
Surveys a period of Russian literature with authors, movements and dated works, checked against literary histories.
Compares works from two Slavic literatures on a shared theme, checked against primary texts.
Builds a profile of a Polish, Czech, Ukrainian or South Slavic author with works and reception, checked against reference sources.
Maps the formation of a national literary canon and its political context, checked against literary histories.
Translates a Slavic literary passage into English preserving style and register, checked by back-translation against the source.
Compares published English translations of a passage and evaluates choices, checked against the source text.
Builds a terminology glossary for a Slavic text with consistent renderings, checked for consistency across the text.
Soviet and Eastern European Film Analyzer
Analyzes form and politics of a Slavic film, checked against film scholarship and production history.
Maps artists, manifestos and works of a Slavic avant-garde movement, checked against dated sources.
Analyzes post-Soviet media narratives on a topic, checked against the original-language sources.
